newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained at a standstill near midday on Friday, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were scattered at $65.00 per cwt and passed again by owners asking $66.00 to $67.00.
Sales following the Memorial Day holiday weekend were light, with about 29,000 head sold this week in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 37,000 in Kansas, sources said.
Sales were at $66.00 on Tuesday before slipping to $65.00 in thin activity Wednesday and Thursday.
Nebraska weekly sales were more active with near 90,000 head sold at $105.00 to $106.00 per cwt on a dressed basis and $65.00/live, the feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle prices this week were pressured by lower beef prices, sources said. Packers were forced to lower beef prices to reduce large inventories in coolers, they said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.31 to down $0.29, with 205 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
Heavyweight choice beef was down $0.01 at $103.56, compared with Thursday, but down $1.05 from last Friday's close, USDA statistics showed.
